title: Why a bulb needs a full loop
body: Electricity only flows when it can go all the way round a loop. It leaves one end of the battery and goes through the bulb. Then it comes back into the other end.
That's why a bulb has two connections. The flow goes in one side and out the other. With only one wire, there's no way back to the battery. So nothing flows and the bulb stays dark.
The battery doesn't fill the bulb up with electricity. The electricity is already in the wires. The battery pushes it round, like a pump pushing water round a ring of pipes.
realWorld: A torch works the same way. Click it on and its switch closes a gap in the loop. Click it off and the gap opens again.
